唱.meaning: On a planet with a double <part>sun</part>, one disc stacked above the other, a choir of frogs opens every <part>mouth</part> at dawn and drones the same three words over and over until both suns are up. At sunset they start again. Their <kanji>chant</kanji> never changes.
唱.on: Tourists buy tickets: it's the best <sound>show</sound> in the swamp.
唱.kun: The lead frog sits on a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, waving a piece of <sound>na</sound>an like a baton.

狭.meaning: Five anglers squeeze into a one-person ice-fishing tent. There's only room to dangle one <part>fishhook</part> through the hole, so the rest stand in a tight <part>group hug</part>, elbows in ears, rods up noses. It's very <kanji>cramped</kanji>.
狭.on: They pass the time dreaming aloud of a roomy holiday in <sound>Kyo</sound>to.
狭.kun: One angler tries to <sound>se</sound>ttle onto a stool, but it turns out to be his <sound>Ma</sound>'s knee.

偏.meaning: The school <part>notice board</part> is meant to be fair, but the caretaker only pins up his own daughter's drawings, and hangs his coat on the <part>coat hook</part> right over everyone else's posters. Nobody else's work gets seen. He's terribly <kanji>partial</kanji>.
偏.on: Even the prize for best drawing goes to his pet <sound>hen</sound>.
偏.kun: The hen sits <sound>ca</sound>lmly on a <sound>ta</sound>co, leaning to one side, pecking <sound>yo</sound>gurt from his spoon.

依.meaning: A wobbly old <part>coat hook</part> is barely screwed into the wall. The only thing holding it up is the heavy wool <part>garment</part> hanging on it, pressed flat against the plaster. If anyone takes that coat, the hook drops. It's completely <kanji>reliant</kanji> on it.
依.on: Inside the coat's pocket lives an <sound>ee</sound>l, who helps by curling its tail round the hook.
依.kun: The eel depends on the spoonfuls of <sound>yo</sound>gurt the owner leaves in the pocket each night.

恵.meaning: Every night a stranger sneaks out and plants <part>one</part> row of seedlings in a widow's empty <part>rice field</part>, then draws a little <part>heart</part> in the mud. By harvest the whole field is green, and nobody has seen who did it. It's a secret <kanji>favor</kanji>.
恵.on: On harvest day she leaves a <sound>ca</sound>ke on the fence post to say thank you.
恵.kun: Next morning the cake is gone, and in its place sits a <sound>me</sound>lon with a note: '<sound>Goo</sound>d luck.'

扱.meaning: A dockworker never lifts a crate by hand. She hooks each one with an <part>anchor</part> and swings it gently into a <part>catch net</part>, not a scratch on it. Eggs, pianos, a sleeping baby elephant: she knows how to <kanji>handle</kanji> anything.
扱.on: Even a slippery bar of <sound>soa</sound>p can't wriggle out of her net.
扱.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>... <sound>tsu</sound>!' she sneezes, and still catches a flying <sound>ca</sound>rp in the net.
